claim: The atom's exact token 'unsupported or already-covered' is not preserved anywhere in the compile, yet ERS-004 lists it in preserved_exact_tokens; the canonical text names three classes in prose and the fourth in snake_case, so the class vocabulary is inconsistent with itself and with the ledger.
evidence: atom-external-research-owner-canon exact_tokens: "unsupported or already-covered". ERS-004 canonical_text: "or unsupported_or_covered, a proposal the product already owns or the evidence does not support" and "unsupported_or_covered is a class of the union, not a false-positive rate." A search of all 18 draft unit texts with preserved_exact_tokens fields removed finds no occurrence of 'unsupported or already-covered'.
suggested_repair: State the class in ERS-004 as 'unsupported or already-covered (unsupported_or_covered)' on first use so the atom's token is preserved and the four class names are written one way.

claim: The atom's exact token 'protocol fingerprint' is not preserved anywhere in the compile, and ERS-014 declares both 'protocol fingerprint' and 'output manifest' as preserved when neither phrase occurs in its text.
evidence: atom-external-research-owner-canon exact_tokens include "protocol fingerprint"; ERS-014 preserved_exact_tokens: ["protocol fingerprint", "runtime identity", "output manifest", "quiesce"]. The text says only "so two runs sharing a fingerprint provably ran identical code" and "Every frozen output tree carries a SHA-256 manifest".
suggested_repair: Write 'protocol fingerprint' and 'output manifest' into ERS-014's canonical text where the concepts first appear.

claim: PLS-023 declares 'standing repair authorization' as a preserved exact token, but neither the unit text nor its acceptance criteria name that authorization; the unit only says a correction 'requires its currentness re-check and independent review', losing the fact that the correction lands under a standing authorization rather than a new one.
evidence: atom-research-landing-ledger-consumer exact_tokens: "standing repair authorization"; PLS-023 preserved_exact_tokens: ["standing repair authorization", "currentness", "independent review"]. PLS-023 canonical_text: "The ledger records the landing; it does not authorize it, because a correction still requires its currentness re-check and independent review and a capability or product choice still requires the user's recorded answer." The phrase 'standing repair authorization' does not occur in PLS-023.
suggested_repair: Say in PLS-023 that a correction lands under the standing repair authorization, which the ledger records and does not supply.

claim: Six units declare preserved_exact_tokens that do not appear in their own text, so the field cannot be used to check token preservation.
evidence: Missing from their own unit text: ERS-002 'reconcile' and 'compare' (text uses 'reconciliation' and 'comparison'); ERS-007 'accepted for planning' and 'unapproved optional capability' (text uses 'a deferred or unapproved item'); ERS-008 'native records' (text uses 'native usage records'); ERS-009 'bound_by' (text uses 'names the limit that bound it'); ERS-013 'same family' (text uses 'shares a model family'); PLS-023 'standing repair authorization'.
suggested_repair: Either write each declared token into the unit text verbatim or remove it from preserved_exact_tokens.

claim: The contract-family atom's third negative constraint, which confines the scripts edit to registration, is dropped: ATS-054 carries the atom's first two negative constraints verbatim and substitutes a different third one, so nothing in canon forbids changing the contracts verifier's behaviour while registering the pair.
evidence: atom-external-research-contract-family negative_constraints: "Do not change any behaviour of the contracts verifier beyond registering this pair." ATS-054 negative_constraints: "Do not infer runtime, provider, recovery, security, visual or performance results from fixture validation.", "Do not add schemas or fixture pairs to the gate through an ambient glob.", "Do not convert static validation into execution evidence or a readiness unlock." The authorization shard likewise admits the pack-list addition "as a registration-only scripts edit".
suggested_repair: Add the atom's constraint to ATS-054 verbatim, keeping the substituted one as a fourth.

claim: The authorization's central rule - promise nothing the experiments did not exercise, and have every promise cite the run that established it - is not compiled as a general obligation in any unit; it survives only as three unit-local negative constraints about latency, cheap-arm recall and model ranking.
evidence: Authorization shard: "The authorization is explicit that nothing may be promised that the experiments did not exercise, and that every promise cites the run that established it." atom-external-research-owner-canon negative_constraints: "Do not promise a stage, bound or figure the September 2026 campaign did not exercise." No unit carries that constraint; ERS-001, the ownership and authority unit, has only the three constraints about a second research authority, findings as authority, and restating other owners' contracts.
suggested_repair: Add the atom's constraint to ERS-001 with an acceptance criterion that every measured figure in this owner names the run that produced it.

claim: ERS-009 states as unqualified canon that per-job limits 'are what ends most jobs', a frequency claim generalized from one frozen case and with no run named, which is the promise the atom forbids.
evidence: ERS-009 canonical_text: "The per-job limits are the live bound in practice: they, not the cost cap, are what ends most jobs." The evidence shard supports only one case: continuation 4's three reconcile jobs 'cut at the 2,400-second per-job limit' and the capped arm that 'stopped 11 of 12 jobs at the ceiling'. atom-external-research-owner-canon: "Do not promise a stage, bound or figure the September 2026 campaign did not exercise." Every other measured claim in the owner (ERS-010, ERS-011, ERS-012) names continuation 4; this one does not.
suggested_repair: Attribute the claim to continuation 4 on the frozen case, or restate it as the reporting rule that a job names the limit that bound it.

claim: SSYS-037 turns the same ungrounded frequency claim into required user-facing Settings copy, so a single frozen case becomes a product statement shown to the user.
evidence: SSYS-037 canonical_text: "Their controls state that the per-job limits, not the cost cap, are what usually ends a job"; acceptance criterion: "The per-job limit controls state that they, not the cost cap, usually end a job." atom-research-limit-values-settings requires only "the per-topic cost cap, the per-job response and time limits, the lifetime cap per arm and the unresolved-usage disposition" as Settings values with their meaning in External Research; it contains no frequency claim, and the evidence shard records no measurement of what ends jobs in general.
suggested_repair: Drop the frequency claim from the required control copy, or qualify it as what the September 2026 campaign observed on one case.

claim: ERS-010's premise that review models 'differ in depth rather than in kind' contradicts ERS-011 in the same owner, and overgeneralizes a result measured between one arm and its own identical control at a different ceiling into a claim about review models generally.
evidence: ERS-010: "because on identical inputs review models differ in depth rather than in kind and a turn-capped arm reports a ceiling, not a judgement." ERS-011: "one of the three, at 0.82 dollars, held three findings no other review arm reached, so the review arms differ in depth and, at the margin, in kind." The evidence shard supports ERS-011 ('the $0.8195 arm held three findings no other review arm reached') and the proper-subset result only for the capped arm against 'its own control - identical inputs, model, effort, admissions, workers and batching'.
suggested_repair: Restate ERS-010's premise as the capped-versus-control proper-subset result for one model at two ceilings, and let ERS-011 carry the across-model finding.

claim: Both open questions say ERS-010 and ERS-012 will be re-adjudicated against continuation 5 'under the currentness rule in ERS-006', but ERS-006's currentness rule is a pre-landing re-check of a correction's cited canon passages; no unit obliges a measured figure already in canon to be re-adjudicated when a later run reports, so the mechanism the ledger relies on does not exist in the compiled canon.
evidence: q-001: "when continuation 5 reports, ERS-010 is re-adjudicated against it under the currentness rule in ERS-006." ERS-006: "a currentness re-check that re-reads every cited passage against live canon and re-adjudicates any passage that moved since the frozen snapshot" - the subject is a correction being landed, not a figure already in canon whose run has been superseded. ERS-012's acceptance criteria require only that figures 'name the run that produced them'.
suggested_repair: Extend ERS-006's currentness rule, or add an acceptance criterion to ERS-010 and ERS-012, so a measured figure is re-adjudicated when a later run of the same measurement reports.

claim: The compile edits a fifth owner document, Plans/Automated_Testing_System.md, that the authorization's enumerated scope does not admit; the authorization names only the research owner, the contracts pair, the three consumer documents and the ledger, and no decision record chooses Automated_Testing_System as the home for the retention unit.
evidence: Authorization shard, 'Scope admitted by this authorization': the owner document, the contracts pair 'added to the contracts verifier's pack list ... as a registration-only scripts edit', 'consumer references in Plans/assistant-chat-design.md, Plans/Planning_Ledger_System.md and Plans/Settings_System.md', and the ledger. compile_queue.json lists 'Plans/Automated_Testing_System.md' in canonical_plan_targets and compiled_owner_docs, and queue-002 compiles ATS-054 into it. dec-002 records only the schema and fixtures materialization and the pack-list registration.
suggested_repair: Record a decision naming Automated_Testing_System as the retaining owner for the contracts pair, or move the retention obligation to a document the authorization admits.

claim: ATS-054, ACD-467 and PLS-023 are compiled as a bare yaml block with no '### <id> - <title>' heading and no trailing ContractRef line, while all fourteen ERS units and the fourth consumer unit SSYS-037 carry both, so three new units are not in the house shape the same compile used everywhere else.
evidence: First and last lines of each draft: ATS-054, ACD-467 and PLS-023 begin '```yaml' and end '```'; ERS-001 through ERS-014 begin '### ERS-0NN - <Title>' and end 'ContractRef: ContractName:...'; SSYS-037 begins '### SSYS-037 - External Research Limit Values' and ends 'ContractRef: ContractName:Plans/Settings_System.md, ...'.
suggested_repair: Give ATS-054, ACD-467 and PLS-023 the same heading and ContractRef trailer the other sixteen units carry.

claim: Three units cite the pilot documents with the '/mnt/Cursor/' prefix stripped, so the lineage entry reads as a repository-relative path that does not resolve from the repository root.
evidence: Evidence shard cites '/mnt/Cursor/PM-Experiments/research-audit-native-20260907/process-pilot-20260908/REVIEW_ADJUDICATION_20260916.md' and the authorization shard cites '/mnt/Cursor/PM-Experiments/.../BRIEF_GOAL3_RESEARCH_CANON_20260917.md'. ERS-010 and ERS-013 source_lineage carry 'PM-Experiments/research-audit-native-20260907/process-pilot-20260908/REVIEW_ADJUDICATION_20260916.md' and ERS-012 carries 'PM-Experiments/research-audit-native-20260907/process-pilot-20260908/BRIEF_GOAL3_RESEARCH_CANON_20260917.md', both without the leading '/mnt/Cursor/'.
suggested_repair: Restore the absolute '/mnt/Cursor/' prefix in the source_lineage of ERS-010, ERS-012 and ERS-013 so the paths match the shards.

claim: ERS-013 announces three obligations and then states four, and its acceptance criteria list five, so the count in canon does not match its own content.
evidence: ERS-013: "An adjudication is truthful only when three obligations hold." The sentences that follow are the credit obligation, the pinned-source code-fact obligation, the shared-family disclosure obligation, and a fourth: "An adjudicator that ran or scored an arm of the same topic may not adjudicate it." acceptance_criteria has five entries.
suggested_repair: Say 'four obligations', or move the reviewer-independence sentence into ERS-006 where the independent-review gate lives.

claim: The atom's negative constraint forbids 'colored border bars'; ACD-467 and ATS-054 both restate it as 'colored status bars', which is a narrower prohibition than the one the atom and the units' own canonical text carry.
evidence: atom-research-packet-chat-consumer negative_constraints: "Do not introduce colored border bars, stripes or emoji glyphs." ACD-467 negative_constraints: "Do not introduce colored status bars, stripes or emoji glyphs." ATS-054 canonical_text: "that a packet cannot be presented all at once or use colored status bars". ACD-467's own canonical_text still says "text status labels with no colored border bars, stripes or emoji glyphs".
suggested_repair: Use the atom's wording, 'colored border bars', in both negative constraints and in the ATS-054 fixture description.

claim: ERS-008 adds a pricing rule - valuation from a published tariff with a floor so captured usage is never zero - that no ledger record, atom or evidence row establishes.
evidence: ERS-008 canonical_text: "a runtime that reports no per-run cost is priced from its native per-response records at the published tariff, floored so captured usage is never recorded as zero." The evidence shard's row for continuation3/gate/cost-policy.json establishes only "Cold allowance, two-job average rule, job-end native valuation, retained unresolved charge, per-job 40 responses and 2,400 seconds, lifetime caps", and atom-external-research-owner-canon's summary says only 'budget accounting and the four user-set limits'. No record mentions a published tariff or a non-zero floor.
suggested_repair: Cite the record that establishes the tariff and floor rule, or drop that clause from ERS-008.

claim: ERS-005 is marked gui_related true with a reason that directly contradicts the GUI classification and reason of the atom it was compiled from.
evidence: atom-external-research-owner-canon: gui_related false, reason "Process, accounting and provenance semantics; the user-visible research surfaces are specified in their UI owners, so this atom is not GUI work." ERS-005, compiled from that atom, sets gui_related true with "The packet and its cards are user-visible chat content produced by this owner, even though the surface contract is owned elsewhere."
suggested_repair: Reconcile the two: either qualify the atom's GUI reason to exempt packet content, or mark ERS-005 non-GUI and leave the GUI obligation to ACD-467.

claim: The dependency graph of the new owner is not internally consistent: unblocks and depends_on disagree in both directions.
evidence: ERS-001 unblocks ERS-002 through ERS-014, but only ERS-002 lists ERS-001 in depends_on. ERS-008 lists depends_on [ERS-002] while ERS-002's unblocks is [ERS-003, ERS-004, ERS-012]. ERS-003 unblocks [ERS-004, ERS-013, ERS-014] while ERS-013's depends_on is [ERS-004, ERS-010].
suggested_repair: Make unblocks the inverse of depends_on across ERS-001 to ERS-014, or state in ERS-001 that unblocks is transitive.

claim: The ledger's own audit reference is cited by path with no SHA-256, which is the discipline PLS-023 requires of every cited research artifact.
evidence: compile_queue.json: "latest_audit_ref": "reports/external-research-canon-20260917/verification.json" with no hash beside it, while PLS-023's acceptance criteria say "Every cited research artifact appears by path and SHA-256 and is not copied into the ledger as canon." The evidence shard hashes all eighteen of its sources.
suggested_repair: Record the SHA-256 of reports/external-research-canon-20260917/verification.json alongside latest_audit_ref.

claim: SSYS-037 declares validation surfaces that cannot reach it, because its owner document is in none of the three governance coverage sets and q-003 defers that with blocks_landing false.
evidence: SSYS-037 validation_surfaces: "python3 scripts/pm-plan-index.py validate", "python3 scripts/pm-plans-verify.py run-gates". open_items.json deferred_governance_validation_errors: "governance coverage targets missing from sharding_config sources: ['Plans/Settings_System.md']", "... from Spec_Lock coverage: ['Plans/External_Research.md', 'Plans/Settings_System.md']", "... from plan_graph coverage: [same]". q-003 records this as open with blocks_landing false.
suggested_repair: Note in q-003 that SSYS-037's declared validation surfaces are inert until Plans/Settings_System.md is added to sharding_config sources.
